anomalies.observed: In the 'USB Programming' block, the FCC native-USB port (USB1) uses R53 = 560 Ω in series with the D- line (USB_DM_FCC), while the otherwise identical NAVC port (USB2) uses R56 = 22 Ω in series with its D- line (USB_DM_NAVC). USB1's D+ series resistor R52 is 22 Ω, matching USB2's R55.
anomalies.expected: Both full-speed USB programming ports are duplicated circuits; each D+/D- line should carry a low series termination (~22-33 Ω) as on the NAVC port (R55/R56 = 22 Ω). A 560 Ω series resistor on a USB FS D- line is far outside the source impedance the host expects.

evidence.quote: Connections sheet, 'USB Programming' block: R52 22 -> USB_DP_FCC, R53 560 -> USB_DM_FCC, R54 560 -> USB_ID_FCC
Connections sheet, 'USB Programming' block: R55 22 -> USB_DP_NAVC, R56 22 -> USB_DM_NAVC, R57 560 -> USB_ID_NAVC

anomalies.impact: The 560 Ω series resistor on the FCC USB programming port's D- line will heavily attenuate/distort the full-speed signalling, preventing proper USB enumeration on the FCC DFU/programming connector (USB1). The NAVC port (USB2) is unaffected, so the asymmetry points to a value error rather than an intentional design choice.

parsed.summary: The build otherwise matches the specification (including the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap, which is a known bug, not an anomaly). The one deviation I can read off the drawing is in the duplicated USB programming section: the FCC port's D- series resistor R53 is 560 Ω whereas the identical NAVC port uses 22 Ω (R56), which would break USB enumeration on the FCC programming connector.
